To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a group of high level re-offending delinquents was identified, (2) these high level re-offendes are characterized by an early onset and a high initial level of offending, (3) the high level group is characterized by more adverse outcomes, (4) the high level re-offender group is difficult to identify based on the characteristics known at the first police contact, (5) high level re-offense is associated with more frequent and severe police reactions

the majority of young male offenders do not escalate in their re-offending, but rather remain low level offenders, and that the most severe re-offending trajectories are associated with the highest risk factors and adverse outcomes.
the majority of early onset offenders desist from offending, but that a substantial minority continues to re-offend at a high level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the heterogeneity of re-offense patterns in a group of male early onset offenders and with the identification of individual and environmental characteristics that predict group membership.
the development of re-offending in early-onset offenders, and the factors that may be associated with this development.

the development of offending patterns in male childhood offenders, the factors that are associated with the development of different offending patterns, and the co-morbidity of offending and other negative outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no clear pattern of risk factors associated with the development of persistent delinquency.
the most severe offenders were older and had a more disadvantaged social background.
high level re-offending is associated with older onset, a disadvantaged background, and a severe initial reaction by the police.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is a small group of high level re-offending offenders, who can be identified early on by a combination of characteristics, but who are hard to distinguish from low level re-offending delinquents.
early onset delinquents are not a homogeneous group, and that different types of early delinquents may have a different risk profile and may require different interventions.
there was no single risk profile of early onset delinquents that would allow to predict the future course of offending.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no simple way to identify those at risk for becoming a high level re-offender.
the police can play a key role in the identification of early onset offenders at risk of persistent offending and other adverse outcomes.
the majority of early onset delinquents do not become chronic offenders.
